question: A set of implementing acts will soon be introduced for the currently applicable Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. The new provisions aim, among other things, to take account of the carbon footprint of electric vehicle batteries.

Decarbonising supply chains and monitoring the entire electric car production process cannot, however, take place in a way that discriminates against countries such as Poland, one of the world’s biggest battery producers that, for historical and economic reasons, is only just starting its energy transition process. 1.

Is the Commission aware that introducing provisions that do not take into account the differences between Member States resulting from historical and economic circumstances is antithetical to supporting solidarity between those countries, and, in the long term, may lead to negative consequences for the EU automotive industry’s efforts to be independent and the EU’s just energy transition?

Is it true that, under the planned new implementing acts, even if a production facility purchases ‘clean energy’ that is guaranteed to come from renewable energy sources, its situation will still not change if the energy mix of the country in which the facility is located is inadequate?

How does the Commission think the forthcoming implementing acts will affect the electromobility sector in terms of the allocation of investments, as well as in terms of job losses and the creation of new jobs in certain EU Member States?
